content.comment_body: When creating a new PI Controller, earlier versions allowed referencing another block as the setpoint. In the latest software update, this option is missing for new PI controllers. I managed to work around it by starting the configuration in the prior version and then opening the project in the latest version. Interestingly, importing an existing PI controller from a previous project retains the reference option, but creating a new one does not include this feature. Has anyone else noticed this? Is there a known software update to address it? After further testing, choosing an older hardware model such as version 6 or 7 shows the reference block feature for PI controllers, but selecting version 8 does not. Does anyone know the reason? It's going to make the current project challenging if assigning an adjustable setpoint to the controller isn’t possible. Any suggestions are appreciated.
With the newer hardware and updated software release, the reference functionality is managed differently. See link: Reference function [version_no] [url]
Thank you, this information is very helpful.
The PI controller for version 8 hardware includes different configuration options such as dead zone, autotuning, and offset.
Please read and respond specifically to the question regarding the reference function, rather than broadly discussing PI controller features.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have observed that referencing another block as the setpoint within the PI Controller is not available for version 8 hardware in the latest software, whereas it is accessible for older hardware models. This highlights inconsistency in user experience and has resulted in confusion and potential workflow challenges.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect PI Controllers in the latest software to provide the capability to reference another block for the setpoint when using version 8 hardware, consistent with previous software and hardware releases.
